create.name: Design Product Experiment
create.description: Design a product experiment that tests a decision-critical hypothesis with a valid comparison, primary metric, guardrails, stopping rule, analysis plan, and follow-up decision. Use when validating a solution, planning an A/B test, testing an assumption, or reviewing whether an experiment can produce decisive evidence.
create.content:
---
name: design-product-experiment
description: Design a product experiment that tests a decision-critical hypothesis with a valid comparison, primary metric, guardrails, stopping rule, analysis plan, and follow-up decision. Use when validating a solution, planning an A/B test, testing an assumption, or reviewing whether an experiment can produce decisive evidence.
---

# Design Product Experiment

## Contract

Design backward from the decision. Test the riskiest claim with the cheapest method that can answer it. Do not use an A/B test when observation, interview, prototype, smoke test, or technical probe is more appropriate.

## Workflow

1. State the decision and falsifiable hypothesis: population, change, expected behavior, mechanism, and time window.
2. Identify the assumption type: value, demand, comprehension, usability, feasibility, viability, or causal impact.
3. Choose the method and comparison. Define assignment unit, eligibility, control, exposure, contamination risks, and novelty effects.
4. Select one primary decision metric with exact calculation and window. Add diagnostic and guardrail metrics.
5. Estimate sample and duration from baseline, minimum meaningful effect, variance, power, seasonality, and traffic; use ranges when inputs are unknown.
6. Predefine exclusions, stopping rules, data-quality checks, segment analysis, and interpretation for positive, negative, null, or inconclusive results.
7. Define the operational plan, owner, ethics or privacy checks, and the decision each result triggers.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signals, survey responses, people or account context, documents, and synthetic persona tests to refine hypotheses. Synthetic results can reveal questions or usability risks but cannot establish real-world causal impact.

## Output

Return decision, hypothesis, method, population, assignment, variants, metrics, sample assumptions, duration, risks, analysis plan, stopping rule, result-to-decision table, and instrumentation checklist.

## Quality Gate

Reject unfalsifiable hypotheses, multiple primary metrics, peeking-based stopping, post-hoc segments presented as confirmed, and tests too underpowered to change the decision.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [experiment-design](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/experiment-design), [product-experiments](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-experiments), and [ab-test-analysis](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-data-analytics/skills/ab-test-analysis).

create.name: Define Product Metrics
create.description: Define a product metric system connecting customer value, a North Star or outcome measure, controllable inputs, guardrails, business effects, and decision rules. Use when choosing KPIs, designing a dashboard, writing success metrics, auditing vanity metrics, or aligning a team on measurement.
create.content:
---
name: define-product-metrics
description: Define a product metric system connecting customer value, a North Star or outcome measure, controllable inputs, guardrails, business effects, and decision rules. Use when choosing KPIs, designing a dashboard, writing success metrics, auditing vanity metrics, or aligning a team on measurement.
---

# Define Product Metrics

## Contract

Metrics exist to change decisions. Tie each measure to a value mechanism and behavior. Distinguish outcomes, leading inputs, health guardrails, diagnostic measures, and business results.

## Workflow

1. State the customer value and product or business decision the metric system supports.
2. Map the causal value loop from eligible user to meaningful outcome.
3. Choose an outcome or North Star measure that reflects delivered value, not mere activity. Define population, event, numerator, denominator, window, and exclusions.
4. Build a small input tree of controllable behaviors that plausibly drive the outcome.
5. Add guardrails for quality, trust, fairness, reliability, cost, and cannibalization.
6. Define segment cuts, baselines, data sources, owners, refresh cadence, and known measurement gaps.
7. Set decision rules and investigation triggers. Separate targets from definitions and document target rationale.
8. Audit for gaming, survivorship, lag, denominator shifts, and vanity metrics.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use signal and tag aggregates, surveys, projects, account evidence, documents, and knowledge pages to define customer-value measures and leading qualitative indicators. Do not claim product analytics data was queried unless a connected source actually provides it.

## Output

Return metric hierarchy, exact definitions, causal map, data sources, segments, owners, baselines, targets or thresholds, guardrails, cadence, decision rules, and instrumentation gaps.

## Quality Gate

Every metric must have a definition, owner, source, and action. Reject totals without denominators, measures easily optimized without value, and dashboards with no decision path.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [metrics-framework](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/metrics-framework), [north-star-metrics](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/north-star-metrics), and [metrics-dashboard](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-product-discovery/skills/metrics-dashboard).

create.name: Write Product Requirements
create.description: Write evidence-linked product requirements that define the problem, target users, outcomes, scope, behavior, quality constraints, success evidence, non-goals, risks, and open decisions without over-specifying implementation. Use when drafting or revising a PRD, product spec, feature brief, or outcome contract.
create.content:
---
name: write-product-requirements
description: Write evidence-linked product requirements that define the problem, target users, outcomes, scope, behavior, quality constraints, success evidence, non-goals, risks, and open decisions without over-specifying implementation. Use when drafting or revising a PRD, product spec, feature brief, or outcome contract.
---

# Write Product Requirements

## Contract

Requirements establish a shared product contract, not a retrospective justification for a chosen solution. Ground claims in evidence, keep outcome separate from implementation, and expose unresolved decisions.

## Workflow

1. Read existing strategy, jobs, research, decisions, system constraints, and neighboring specs before asking for missing context.
2. Define the problem, affected segment, situation, evidence, and consequence.
3. State desired outcomes, success evidence, and strategic contribution.
4. Describe the user journey or scenarios and write prioritized, testable product behavior.
5. Define quality attributes and constraints: accessibility, privacy, trust, reliability, performance, compatibility, compliance, and operations as relevant.
6. State non-goals, dependencies, assumptions, risks, rollout, measurement, and unresolved questions.
7. Link evidence and decisions. Mark facts, hypotheses, commitments, and proposals distinctly.
8. Review for altitude, contradictions, ambiguity, solution leakage, and verifiability.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use calls, signals, surveys, documents, knowledge pages, projects, triage, and linked tickets to ground the problem and avoid duplicate work. Mutating project state still requires explicit approval.

## Output

Return a concise requirements document plus an evidence ledger, open-decision list, assumption register, and acceptance or outcome scenarios.

## Quality Gate

Every requirement must be necessary, comprehensible, and verifiable. Remove unsupported urgency, feature requests presented as needs, implementation details that belong in design, and hidden non-goals.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [create-product-spec](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/create-product-spec), [prd-writing](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/prd-writing), [writing-prds](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/writing-prds), and [create-prd](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/create-prd).

create.name: Scope Product Release
create.description: Reduce a product release to the smallest coherent outcome while preserving trust, usability, measurement, and operational safety. Use when defining an MVP, cutting scope, responding to a deadline, splitting a feature, or deciding what can move to a later release.
create.content:
---
name: scope-product-release
description: Reduce a product release to the smallest coherent outcome while preserving trust, usability, measurement, and operational safety. Use when defining an MVP, cutting scope, responding to a deadline, splitting a feature, or deciding what can move to a later release.
---

# Scope Product Release

## Contract

Cut breadth, automation, polish, scale, or variants before cutting the core outcome. A smaller release must still complete a real job for a defined user. Revisit the bet when the constraint changes materially.

## Workflow

1. Re-state the target user, situation, must-deliver outcome, success evidence, appetite, and fixed constraints.
2. Map the end-to-end journey and identify the thin coherent path that delivers value.
3. Classify scope as essential outcome, trust or safety, learning instrumentation, accelerator, edge case, or future option.
4. Explore reductions by segment, use case, channel, platform, geography, data type, automation, configuration, integration, scale, or service level.
5. Preserve accessibility, privacy, security, compliance, reliability, supportability, rollback, and measurement at the required risk level.
6. Split follow-ons by dependency and learning, not arbitrary phase labels.
7. Document cuts, consequences, manual operations, upgrade path, re-entry criteria, and who accepted each tradeoff.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use strongest customer evidence, project detail, triage, linked tickets, documents, and prior decisions to protect the core outcome and identify low-evidence scope. Do not alter project records without explicit approval.

## Output

Return the core outcome, thin journey, in-scope and out-of-scope tables, cut rationale, preserved quality gates, manual operations, dependencies, follow-ons, and release acceptance evidence.

## Quality Gate

Reject a release that cannot complete the job, creates unrecoverable trust debt, or hides essential work in an undefined later phase.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [scope-cutting](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/scope-cutting), [shipping-velocity](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/shipping-velocity), and [epic-breakdown-advisor](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/epic-breakdown-advisor), used as reference only.

create.name: Plan Outcome Roadmap
create.description: Build an outcome-oriented roadmap that connects strategy, customer problems, bets, learning, dependencies, and evidence without presenting distant feature promises as certainty. Use when creating a roadmap, sequencing initiatives, translating strategy into horizons, or revising plans after new evidence.
create.content:
---
name: plan-outcome-roadmap
description: Build an outcome-oriented roadmap that connects strategy, customer problems, bets, learning, dependencies, and evidence without presenting distant feature promises as certainty. Use when creating a roadmap, sequencing initiatives, translating strategy into horizons, or revising plans after new evidence.
---

# Plan Outcome Roadmap

## Contract

Roadmap outcomes and decisions, not a feature calendar. Confidence must decrease with distance. Separate commitments, shaped bets, options, obligations, and discovery work.

## Workflow

1. Establish strategic outcomes, constraints, planning horizon, capacity, obligations, and decision cadence.
2. Normalize candidate work into outcomes or customer opportunities; separate mandatory risk or maintenance work.
3. Attach evidence, owner, target segment, leading measure, confidence, dependencies, and key assumptions.
4. Prioritize and sequence by strategic contribution, urgency, learning, dependency, risk, and portfolio balance.
5. Place items into Now, Next, and Later or equivalent horizons with explicit entry criteria. Use dates only for true commitments or constraints.
6. Define discovery and decision gates before moving an item closer.
7. Record deferrals, tradeoffs, capacity allocation, and change triggers. Establish a regular evidence-based review.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use project types, projects, triage, linked tickets, signals, surveys, documents, and prior decisions. Treat observed tool state as evidence; promotion or project mutation requires explicit approval.

## Output

Return roadmap principles, horizon table, outcome and evidence per item, confidence, measures, dependencies, capacity allocation, obligations lane, deferrals, decision gates, and review cadence.

## Quality Gate

Reject distant feature commitments, items with no outcome or evidence, overloaded Now horizons, and roadmaps that omit maintenance, compliance, or learning capacity.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [roadmap-planning](https://github.com/assimovt/productskills/tree/main/skills/roadmap-planning), [roadmap-prioritization](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/roadmap-prioritization), and [outcome-roadmap](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/outcome-roadmap).

create.name: Run Product Premortem
create.description: Run a structured premortem on a product bet, requirements document, rollout, migration, or launch and convert plausible failure modes into mitigations, owners, triggers, and contingency plans. Use when stress-testing a plan, preparing a launch, exposing hidden concerns, or deciding whether risk is acceptable.
create.content:
---
name: run-product-premortem
description: Run a structured premortem on a product bet, requirements document, rollout, migration, or launch and convert plausible failure modes into mitigations, owners, triggers, and contingency plans. Use when stress-testing a plan, preparing a launch, exposing hidden concerns, or deciding whether risk is acceptable.
---

# Run Product Premortem

## Contract

Assume the effort failed at a specific future point and reason backward. Cover customer, product, engineering, data, operations, go-to-market, legal, security, accessibility, finance, and organizational failure. Distinguish evidence-backed risk from anxiety.

## Workflow

1. Define the plan, intended outcome, launch or decision point, scope, assumptions, and risk tolerance.
2. Write a concrete failure narrative: what customers and the business observe after failure.
3. Generate failure modes independently across functions before group convergence.
4. For each mode, record cause, affected party, evidence, likelihood range, severity, detectability, timing, and dependency.
5. Identify correlated risks, cascading failures, silent failures, and assumptions nobody owns.
6. Classify actions as prevent, detect, contain, recover, accept, or transfer. Name owner, due point, leading trigger, and proof of completion.
7. Separate launch blockers, bounded fast follows, monitored risks, and low-value concerns. Define rollback and escalation.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Review customer evidence, project detail, linked tickets, documents, knowledge gaps, prior launches, and related signals. Any recheck, attachment, or project mutation requires explicit approval.

## Output

Return failure narrative, risk register, correlated risks, mitigations, owners, triggers, blocker decision, contingency and rollback plan, accepted risks, and unresolved questions.

## Quality Gate

Reject vague risks, mitigations without owners or verification, universal high ratings, and lists that ignore customer harm or operational recovery.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [pre-mortem](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/pre-mortem) and [high-stakes-decisions](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/high-stakes-decisions).

create.name: Align Product Stakeholders
create.description: Map stakeholders, incentives, decision rights, conflicts, evidence needs, and communication paths for a product decision or initiative. Use when preparing alignment, resolving cross-functional disagreement, planning an executive review, clarifying ownership, or preventing consensus theater.
create.content:
---
name: align-product-stakeholders
description: Map stakeholders, incentives, decision rights, conflicts, evidence needs, and communication paths for a product decision or initiative. Use when preparing alignment, resolving cross-functional disagreement, planning an executive review, clarifying ownership, or preventing consensus theater.
---

# Align Product Stakeholders

## Contract

Aim for decision clarity and durable commitment, not unanimous enthusiasm. Surface incentives, constraints, and disagreements early. Never attribute a position to someone without evidence.

## Workflow

1. Define the decision, scope, deadline, decision owner, contributors, consulted parties, and affected groups.
2. Map each stakeholder's goals, incentives, risks, authority, knowledge, dependencies, preferred evidence, and current position.
3. Identify true conflicts: goals, facts, risk tolerance, sequencing, resources, or unclear rights.
4. Gather missing evidence and distinguish resolvable factual disputes from value or priority choices.
5. Choose engagement: inform, consult, co-create, negotiate, or escalate. Sequence conversations to reduce surprise without forming hidden coalitions.
6. Prepare a pre-read with decision, context, options, tradeoffs, recommendation, dissent, and explicit asks.
7. Record the decision, owner, commitments, unresolved dissent, communication plan, and review trigger.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use documents, knowledge pages, project evidence, calls, and linked artifacts to establish prior decisions and customer impact. Do not infer private motivations from CRM or conversation data.

## Output

Return stakeholder map, decision rights, conflict diagnosis, evidence gaps, engagement sequence, pre-read outline, meeting decision frame, commitments, dissent, and communication plan.

## Quality Gate

Reject broad labels such as resistant or supportive without evidence, meetings with no decision, and alignment plans that hide tradeoffs or omit affected customers.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [stakeholder-alignment](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/stakeholder-alignment), [stakeholder-map](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-execution/skills/stakeholder-map), and [stakeholder-mapping](https://github.com/deanpeters/Product-Manager-Skills/tree/main/skills/stakeholder-mapping), used as reference only.

create.name: Verify Product Outcomes
create.description: Compare implemented and observed product behavior against intended customer outcomes, requirements, quality constraints, and release evidence. Use when implementation or deployment is complete, during UAT, while reviewing intended versus implemented behavior, or before declaring a feature complete.
create.content:
---
name: verify-product-outcomes
description: Compare implemented and observed product behavior against intended customer outcomes, requirements, quality constraints, and release evidence. Use when implementation or deployment is complete, during UAT, while reviewing intended versus implemented behavior, or before declaring a feature complete.
---

# Verify Product Outcomes

## Contract

Verification is evidence, not a claim. Distinguish code complete, tests passed, deployed, observed, customer validated, and outcome achieved. Verify the user journey and failure paths, not only the happy-path implementation.

## Workflow

1. Resolve the authoritative requirements, decision records, designs, acceptance scenarios, release artifact, environment, and exact version or SHA.
2. Convert intended outcomes and constraints into a traceability matrix with observable evidence.
3. Inspect the implemented surface and supporting behavior. Test primary journeys, permissions, empty and error states, accessibility, recovery, analytics, and operational controls.
4. Compare artifact intent, implementation, automated checks, environment state, and observed behavior. Record evidence links, screenshots, logs, or IDs.
5. Classify gaps as missing requirement, implementation divergence, regression, ambiguous spec, instrumentation gap, or accepted tradeoff.
6. Assess severity from customer outcome and risk, not code size.
7. Produce a verdict per requirement and an overall verified, conditional, or failed state. Name what remains unverified.

## BuildBetter Acceleration

If BuildBetter MCP is available, search organization skills first. Use projects, linked tickets, evidence, documents, signals, surveys, and agent-session or release context when deployed. Keep BuildBetter evidence distinct from browser, test, CI, staging, and production proof.

## Output

Return exact artifact and environment identifiers, traceability matrix, evidence, gaps, severity, verdict, remaining unknowns, and required follow-ups.

## Quality Gate

Never infer production behavior from a branch, staging from CI, customer validation from UAT, or outcome achievement from shipment. Missing evidence stays missing.

## Provenance

Independently authored. Informed by [uat-ux-debug](https://github.com/mekenthompson/ProductOS/tree/main/skills/uat-ux-debug), [intended-vs-implemented](https://github.com/phuryn/pm-skills/tree/main/pm-ai-shipping/skills/intended-vs-implemented), and [product-reviews](https://github.com/RefoundAI/lenny-skills/tree/main/skills/product-reviews).
